method: Every visitor-facing field is split into exact contiguous segments. Each segment is counted by the recorded Unicode word matcher and marked source-derived or LAiDIES-authored. The sole Anthropic allocation includes conservative source-gap and provider-claim qualifications.

segments.text: Claude raises usage limits for paying subscribers
segments.reason: The subscription-limit change derives from the Anthropic announcement.

segments.text: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22.
With the launch, it says it raised five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans.
A usage limit is the amount a plan lets you use within a stated time window.
A higher limit may mean more use before you have to wait for the five-hour allowance to reset.
segments.reason: Conservative ordinary-reader consequence of a higher time-windowed limit.

segments.text: Anthropic does not say how much more or promise a message count.
segments.reason: Bounded absence established by the complete source reread.

segments.text: Anthropic also says subscription users get a rate-limit reset they can save and use when they choose.
Separately, developers paying Anthropic directly for API use — a software connection to a model — pay $4 for input and $20 for output per million tokens.
segments.reason: API product boundary, plain definition and published token prices.

segments.text: Those are usage charges based on text processed, not monthly Claude subscription prices.
segments.reason: Necessary scope boundary for the published API prices.

segments.text: If you use one of the named plans, check your current plan details and model selector to see what limit and model access apply to your account.
segments.reason: LAiDIES action following from the unresolved account-specific gap.

segments.text: The announcement does not map ordinary Claude-chat access plan by plan.
segments.reason: Bounded absence established by the complete source reread.

segments.text: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 can take on long software jobs such as moving a project to a new system or reviewing its code.
Compared with Fable 5.1, Anthropic says Opus 5.5 performs similarly on most work.
That does not show Opus 5.5 is necessary for a routine email or summary; another Claude model may be enough.
Anthropic’s performance, speed, safety and cost-per-task claims are not independently validated here.
segments.reason: Attribution and evidence-limit statement tied to the provider announcement.

segments.text: “Anthropic raised five-hour usage limits on four paid plan types and added a saveable reset.
It did not publish the size of each increase or a message count.”
Working with AI 101 §7.4 — Free vs Paid (The Honest Answer) explains why the model, product surface and plan are separate choices — and why current access should be checked instead of remembered.
segments.reason: Governed LAiDIES learning link, not an Anthropic finding.
